variables.title: Store an integer
variables.task: Read one integer into an int variable and print that value.
variables.hint: An int holds a whole number.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One integer n.
details.output: Print n on one line.

examples.explanation: The variable n stores 0, so printing n produces 0.
The variable n stores -1000000, so printing n produces -1000000.
The variable n stores 1000000, so printing n produces 1000000.

variables.title: Store a large count
variables.task: Read a whole number that can exceed the int range. Store it in a long and print it.
variables.hint: Use nextLong and a long variable.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One integer count.
details.output: Print count.

examples.explanation: The long variable preserves all the digits of 0; the output is 0.
The long variable preserves all the digits of -1000000000000; the output is -1000000000000.
The long variable preserves all the digits of 1000000000000; the output is 1000000000000.

variables.title: Store a decimal reading
variables.task: Read a decimal reading into a double and display exactly two digits after the decimal point.
variables.hint: Use a double variable and %.2f.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One decimal reading with exactly two digits after the decimal point.
details.output: Print the reading with exactly two decimal places.
constraints: The input has exactly two decimal places.

examples.explanation: The reading is 0.00; two decimal places display it as 0.00.
The reading is -12.34; two decimal places display it as -12.34.
The reading is 10000.00; two decimal places display it as 10000.00.

variables.title: Store a word
variables.task: Store one word in a String variable and print it unchanged.
variables.hint: Use String and next().

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One lowercase word.
details.output: Print the word.
constraints: The word contains 1 to 12 lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The String variable contains "java"; printing it keeps every letter in the same order.
The String variable contains "mira"; printing it keeps every letter in the same order.
The String variable contains "hello"; printing it keeps every letter in the same order.

variables.title: Store a character
variables.task: Read one visible ASCII character, store it in a char variable, and print it.
variables.hint: Read the token and take character 0.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One character.
details.output: Print the same character.
constraints: The character has ASCII code 33 through 126; spaces are excluded.

examples.explanation: The single character stored in symbol is 'A'; that is the character printed.
The single character stored in symbol is '7'; that is the character printed.
The single character stored in symbol is '~'; that is the character printed.

variables.title: Store an enabled setting
variables.task: Read a setting name and a boolean value. Print the name followed by its stored boolean value.
variables.hint: Use nextBoolean() for the second token.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: A name and a boolean, separated by whitespace.
details.output: Print name, one space, then true or false.
constraints: The name is an alphanumeric token of 1 to 12 characters.
The boolean is exactly true or false.

examples.explanation: The name is Ada and enabled stores true, so the two stored values produce "Ada true".
The name is Bo and enabled stores false, so the two stored values produce "Bo false".
The name is Cleo and enabled stores true, so the two stored values produce "Cleo true".

variables.title: Keep two measurements separate
variables.task: Read length and width into separate variables. Print width first and length second.
variables.hint: Give each input a distinct variable name.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: length width.
details.output: Print width and length separated by one space.

examples.explanation: length is 0 and width is 7; width comes first in the requested output, giving 7 0.
length is 12 and width is 4; width comes first in the requested output, giving 4 12.
length is 10000 and width is 0; width comes first in the requested output, giving 0 10000.

variables.title: Keep a typed record
variables.task: Read an integer ID, a word, and a boolean. Print the word, the ID, and the boolean in that order.
variables.hint: Use int, String, and boolean variables.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Three tokens: id word active.
details.output: Print word id active, separated by single spaces.
constraints: word has 1 to 12 lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The record stores ID 0, word java, and active=false. Reordering these fields gives "java 0 false".
The record stores ID 42, word mira, and active=true. Reordering these fields gives "mira 42 true".
The record stores ID 1000000, word hello, and active=false. Reordering these fields gives "hello 1000000 false".

variables.title: Copy a stored value
variables.task: Read a number into original, copy it into backup, and print both variables on separate lines.
variables.hint: Assignment copies the current value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One integer original.
details.output: Print original, then backup on the next line.

examples.explanation: Copying original=0 makes backup=0. Both lines therefore contain 0.
Copying original=-15 makes backup=-15. Both lines therefore contain -15.
Copying original=100000 makes backup=100000. Both lines therefore contain 100000.

variables.title: Replace a current value
variables.task: Read an old value and a replacement. Assign the replacement to the current variable and print its final value.
variables.hint: The later assignment replaces the earlier value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: old replacement.
details.output: Print the final current value.

examples.explanation: current starts at 5. Assigning replacement=0 changes current to 0.
current starts at -12. Assigning replacement=8 changes current to 8.
current starts at 100000. Assigning replacement=-100000 changes current to -100000.

variables.title: Increase a counter
variables.task: Read a starting counter and an increase. Use the increase to update the counter, then print it.
variables.hint: counter += increase adds to the stored value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: counter increase.
details.output: Print the updated counter.

examples.explanation: The counter starts at 0; adding 0 changes it to 0 + 0 = 0.
The counter starts at 7; adding 3 changes it to 7 + 3 = 10.
The counter starts at 1000000; adding 1000000 changes it to 1000000 + 1000000 = 2000000.

variables.title: Decrease a balance
variables.task: Read a balance and a charge. Subtract the charge from the stored balance, allowing a negative result.
variables.hint: balance -= charge updates balance.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: balance charge.
details.output: Print the updated balance.

examples.explanation: Subtracting charge 0 from balance 0 leaves 0.
Subtracting charge 15 from balance 10 leaves -5.
Subtracting charge 1 from balance 1000000 leaves 999999.

variables.title: Scale a stored count
variables.task: Read a count and a multiplier. Multiply the stored count by the multiplier and print it.
variables.hint: Use *= to replace count with the product.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: count multiplier.
details.output: Print the updated count.

examples.explanation: Multiplying the stored count 0 by 5 replaces it with 0.
Multiplying the stored count -7 by 3 replaces it with -21.
Multiplying the stored count 10000 by 100 replaces it with 1000000.

variables.title: Divide a stored quantity
variables.task: Read a nonnegative quantity and a positive divisor. Replace the quantity with its whole-number quotient.
variables.hint: An int divided by an int gives a whole-number quotient.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: quantity divisor.
details.output: Print the quotient; discard any remainder.

examples.explanation: 0 divided by 1 has whole-number quotient 0; that quotient becomes quantity.
17 divided by 5 has whole-number quotient 3; that quotient becomes quantity.
1000000 divided by 1000 has whole-number quotient 1000; that quotient becomes quantity.

variables.title: Retain the leftover amount
variables.task: Read a nonnegative amount and a positive package size. Replace amount with the remainder after forming full packages.
variables.hint: Use %= to store the remainder.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: amount size.
details.output: Print the remainder.

examples.explanation: 0 forms 0 full groups of 8, leaving 0; amount stores that leftover.
17 forms 3 full groups of 5, leaving 2; amount stores that leftover.
1000000 forms 1000 full groups of 1000, leaving 0; amount stores that leftover.

variables.title: Swap two variables
variables.task: Read a and b. Swap their stored values using a temporary variable, then print a followed by b.
variables.hint: Save a before assigning b to it.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: a b.
details.output: Print the swapped a and b separated by one space.

examples.explanation: The temporary variable keeps 0; a becomes 7 and b receives the saved 0, producing 7 0.
The temporary variable keeps -4; a becomes 9 and b receives the saved -4, producing 9 -4.
The temporary variable keeps 1000000; a becomes -1000000 and b receives the saved 1000000, producing -1000000 1000000.

variables.title: Rotate three variables
variables.task: Read a, b, and c. Rotate their stored values so a gets old c, b gets old a, and c gets old b.
variables.hint: Save old c, then assign from right to left.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Three integers: a b c.
details.output: Print the final a b c, separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Old values are (1, 2, 3). Moving old c to a, old a to b, and old b to c gives 3 1 2.
Old values are (0, -4, 8). Moving old c to a, old a to b, and old b to c gives 8 0 -4.
Old values are (10000, 0, -10000). Moving old c to a, old a to b, and old b to c gives -10000 10000 0.

variables.title: Preserve a snapshot
variables.task: Read a starting value and a change. Copy the starting value into snapshot, update current by the change, then print snapshot and current.
variables.hint: Changing current does not change the copied primitive value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: start change.
details.output: Print snapshot and final current separated by one space.

examples.explanation: snapshot keeps 0. current changes by 5 to 5, so the output is 0 5.
snapshot keeps 10. current changes by -3 to 7, so the output is 10 7.
snapshot keeps -1000000. current changes by 1000000 to 0, so the output is -1000000 0.

variables.title: Apply two balance updates
variables.task: Read an opening balance, a deposit, and a withdrawal. Apply the deposit first and the withdrawal second to one balance variable.
variables.hint: Update the same variable in the stated order.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Three integers: opening deposit withdrawal.
details.output: Print the final balance.
constraints: A negative final balance is allowed.

examples.explanation: The deposit changes 0 to 0; withdrawing 0 then leaves 0.
The deposit changes 100 to 140; withdrawing 25 then leaves 115.
The deposit changes 0 to 5; withdrawing 10 then leaves -5.

variables.title: Truncate a decimal to int
variables.task: Read a decimal with one digit after the point. Cast it to int and print the result. Casting discards the fractional part toward zero.
variables.hint: A cast to int truncates toward zero, including negative inputs.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One decimal value with exactly one decimal place.
details.output: Print the int obtained by truncating toward zero.

examples.explanation: Discarding the fractional part of 0.0 toward zero gives 0.
Discarding the fractional part of -3.7 toward zero gives -3.
Discarding the fractional part of 9.9 toward zero gives 9.

variables.title: Promote before multiplying
variables.task: Read two nonnegative int-sized factors. Store their full product in a long so the multiplication does not overflow int.
variables.hint: Convert a factor to long before the multiplication.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: a b.
details.output: Print the exact product.

examples.explanation: 0 × 1000000000 = 0. Promoting a factor to long preserves the full product.
50000 × 50000 = 2500000000. Promoting a factor to long preserves the full product.
1000000000 × 1000000000 = 1000000000000000000. Promoting a factor to long preserves the full product.

variables.title: Keep a fractional average
variables.task: Read two integers. Store their average in a double and print it with exactly one decimal place.
variables.hint: Divide by 2.0 to keep the fractional half.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: a b.
details.output: Print their average with one digit after the decimal point.

examples.explanation: The sum is 0; dividing by 2.0 gives average 0.0.
The sum is 5; dividing by 2.0 gives average 2.5.
The sum is -3; dividing by 2.0 gives average -1.5.

variables.title: Read a character code
variables.task: Read one visible ASCII character. Assign its numeric character code to an int and print that code.
variables.hint: A char can widen to an int code.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One visible ASCII character.
details.output: Print its ASCII code.
constraints: The character has ASCII code 33 through 126.

examples.explanation: The ASCII code of 'A' is 65, so code is printed as 65.
The ASCII code of '0' is 48, so code is printed as 48.
The ASCII code of '~' is 126, so code is printed as 126.

variables.title: Make a character from a code
variables.task: Read an ASCII code and cast it to char. Print the corresponding visible character.
variables.hint: Cast the numeric code to char.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One integer code.
details.output: Print the character with that ASCII code.

examples.explanation: ASCII code 65 corresponds to 'A', which is the character printed.
ASCII code 48 corresponds to '0', which is the character printed.
ASCII code 126 corresponds to '~', which is the character printed.

variables.title: Advance a lowercase letter
variables.task: Read a lowercase letter and a shift. Move forward through the 26-letter alphabet, wrapping after z.
variables.hint: Convert the letter to a zero-based position, add, wrap, then cast back.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: A lowercase letter and an integer shift.
details.output: Print the shifted lowercase letter.
constraints: The letter is a through z.

examples.explanation: a has zero-based alphabet position 0. Adding 0 and wrapping modulo 26 gives position 0, the letter a.
z has zero-based alphabet position 25. Adding 1 and wrapping modulo 26 gives position 0, the letter a.
m has zero-based alphabet position 12. Adding 25 and wrapping modulo 26 gives position 11, the letter l.

variables.title: Use a named conversion constant
variables.task: Read a number of weeks and extra days. Use a final constant of 7 days per week to calculate total days.
variables.hint: A final variable gives the conversion factor a name.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: weeks extraDays.
details.output: Print the total number of days.

examples.explanation: 0 weeks contain 0 days; adding 0 extra days gives 0.
2 weeks contain 14 days; adding 3 extra days gives 17.
1000000 weeks contain 7000000 days; adding 6 extra days gives 7000006.

variables.title: Invert a stored setting
variables.task: Read a setting name and its boolean value. Replace the boolean with its opposite, then print the name and updated value.
variables.hint: The ! operator produces the opposite boolean value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: A name and a boolean.
details.output: Print name followed by the inverted boolean, separated by one space.
constraints: The name is an alphanumeric token of 1 to 12 characters.
The boolean is true or false.

examples.explanation: Ada starts with enabled=true; inversion changes it to false, giving "Ada false".
Bo starts with enabled=false; inversion changes it to true, giving "Bo true".
Cleo starts with enabled=false; inversion changes it to true, giving "Cleo true".

variables.title: Capture postfix and prefix results
variables.task: Read n. First assign old = n++. Then assign updated = ++n. Print old, updated, and final n.
variables.hint: Postfix returns the previous value; prefix returns the changed value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One integer n.
details.output: Print old updated n separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: old receives 0 before n increases to 1. The prefix step increases n to 2 and stores that in updated, producing 0 2 2.
old receives -2 before n increases to -1. The prefix step increases n to 0 and stores that in updated, producing -2 0 0.
old receives 1000000 before n increases to 1000001. The prefix step increases n to 1000002 and stores that in updated, producing 1000000 1000002 1000002.

variables.title: Preserve integer and decimal quotients
variables.task: Read a nonnegative numerator and a positive denominator. Store one quotient as int using integer division and another as double using a cast.
variables.hint: Cast before dividing to produce the double result.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: numerator denominator.
details.output: Print the integer quotient on the first line and the decimal quotient with exactly three decimal places on the second.

examples.explanation: Integer division gives 0. Casting before 0 / 1 preserves the fractional value, displayed as 0.000.
Integer division gives 3. Casting before 7 / 2 preserves the fractional value, displayed as 3.500.
Integer division gives 2. Casting before 99 / 40 preserves the fractional value, displayed as 2.475.

variables.title: Narrow an unsigned-sized value
variables.task: Read a long value from 0 through 4,294,967,295 and cast it to int. Print the signed int value with the same low 32 bits. Values above 2,147,483,647 become value − 4,294,967,296.
variables.hint: A narrowing cast keeps the low 32 bits.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One long integer value.
details.output: Print the signed 32-bit result of the cast.

examples.explanation: 0 fits the nonnegative int range, so the cast keeps it.
2147483648 exceeds the signed int maximum; subtracting 4,294,967,296 gives -2147483648.
4294967295 exceeds the signed int maximum; subtracting 4,294,967,296 gives -1.

variables.title: Store an updated byte
variables.task: Read a signed byte value and an integer change. Add them, then cast the sum to byte. Print the resulting signed byte value. The result wraps into −128 through 127 in steps of 256.
variables.hint: The addition uses int; an explicit byte cast narrows its result.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers: value change.
details.output: Print the signed byte result.

examples.explanation: The sum before casting is 0. Wrapping that sum into the byte range −128 through 127 yields 0.
The sum before casting is 128. Wrapping that sum into the byte range −128 through 127 yields -128.
The sum before casting is -129. Wrapping that sum into the byte range −128 through 127 yields 127.

variables.title: Convert three digit characters
variables.task: Read three separate digit characters. Convert each character into its numeric digit value, then combine them into a three-position decimal number. Leading zeroes do not appear in the numeric output.
variables.hint: Subtract the character code of 0 to obtain each numeric digit.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Three digit characters separated by spaces: hundreds tens ones.
details.output: Print the integer represented by the three digits.

examples.explanation: The digit values are 0, 0, and 0; 0 × 100 + 0 × 10 + 0 = 0.
The digit values are 0, 4, and 2; 0 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 2 = 42.
The digit values are 9, 9, and 9; 9 × 100 + 9 × 10 + 9 = 999.

input-output.title: Print a greeting
input-output.task: Read one name and greet that person.
input-output.hint: Read the fixed inputs in order, then print exactly the requested format.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One name of 1 to 12 letters or digits.
details.output: Print Hello, name!
constraints: Follow the field sizes stated in the input format.

examples.explanation: Insert the name Ada after "Hello, " and add an exclamation mark: Hello, Ada!.
Insert the name Bo after "Hello, " and add an exclamation mark: Hello, Bo!.
Insert the name Cleo after "Hello, " and add an exclamation mark: Hello, Cleo!.

input-output.title: Echo one whole line
input-output.task: Read a whole line, including spaces, and print it unchanged.
input-output.hint: Read the fixed inputs in order, then print exactly the requested format.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: One line of 0 to 80 characters; the line may be empty.
details.output: Print the same line.
constraints: Follow the field sizes stated in the input format.

examples.explanation: The line contains 0 characters. nextLine() retains the spaces inside it.
The line contains 11 characters. nextLine() retains the spaces inside it.
The line contains 8 characters. nextLine() retains the spaces inside it.

input-output.title: Print two tokens on separate lines
input-output.task: Read two words from the input. Print one word per line in the same order.
input-output.hint: Read the fixed inputs in order, then print exactly the requested format.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two lowercase words, each 1 to 12 letters, separated by whitespace.
details.output: Print the first word on line 1 and the second on line 2.
constraints: Follow the field sizes stated in the input format.

examples.explanation: The two tokens are java and code; each receives its own output line.
The two tokens are hello and world; each receives its own output line.
The two tokens are aa and ab; each receives its own output line.

input-output.title: Join three separate lines
input-output.task: Read three complete lines. Join them with the separator " | ". Keep spaces inside each line.

details.output: Print a double quote, the message, and a closing double quote.
constraints: Follow the field sizes stated in the input format.

loops.title: Longest Positive Run

loops.title: Collatz Step Counter
loops.task: Starting with positive n, repeatedly divide by 2 if even or replace it with 3n + 1 if odd. Count the operations required to reach 1. For the stated inputs, the process reaches 1.

loops.title: Armstrong Number Check

8 is 8. Mark used powers with 1 and other positions with 0 to obtain 1000.

methods.title: Count Binary Ones
methods.task: Return the number of 1 digits in the binary representation of n. Use repeated integer division and remainder inside the method. Define and call static int countOnes(int n).
methods.hint: Remainder modulo 2 reveals one binary digit each iteration.

requirements: Define the specified method(s). Have main call the method that produces the result, using any additional helpers as described.
Read input in the stated order. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: One nonnegative integer n.
details.output: Print the returned result on one line.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 1000000000. Do not use built-in bit-counting methods.

examples.explanation: 13 in binary is 1101. It contains 3 digits equal to 1.
0 in binary is 0. It contains 0 digits equal to 1.
8 in binary is 1000. It contains 1 digits equal to 1.

methods.title: Combine Three Digits
methods.task: Return the integer formed by hundreds, tens, and units. A leading zero does not appear in the numeric output. Define and call static int combineDigits(int hundreds,int tens,int units).
methods.hint: Multiply each digit by its decimal place value before adding.

requirements: Define the specified method(s). Have main call the method that produces the result, using any additional helpers as described.
Read input in the stated order. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: Three integers hundreds, tens, units.
details.output: Print the returned result on one line.

examples.explanation: The place values contribute 400, 0, and 7. Their sum is 407; numeric output omits leading zeroes.
The place values contribute 0, 0, and 3. Their sum is 3; numeric output omits leading zeroes.
The place values contribute 0, 0, and 0. Their sum is 0; numeric output omits leading zeroes.

methods.title: Next Strict Multiple
methods.task: Return the smallest integer strictly greater than n that is divisible by positive divisor. If n is already a multiple, advance to the next one. Define and call static int nextMultiple(int n,int divisor).
methods.hint: Normalize a negative remainder, then move forward by divisor − remainder.

requirements: Define the specified method(s). Have main call the method that produces the result, using any additional helpers as described.
Read input in the stated order. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: Two integers n and divisor.
details.output: Print the returned result on one line.

examples.explanation: The consecutive multiples around the answer are 12 and 16. The first is ≤ 12, and 16 is strictly greater, so return 16.
The consecutive multiples around the answer are -8 and -4. The first is ≤ -7, and -4 is strictly greater, so return -4.
The consecutive multiples around the answer are -8 and -4. The first is ≤ -8, and -4 is strictly greater, so return -4.

methods.title: Time Difference through a Helper
methods.task: Convert each time to seconds after midnight using toSeconds. Return the absolute difference between the two times; do not wrap across midnight. Define and call static int toSeconds(int h,int m,int s); static int timeDifference(int h1,int m1,int s1,int h2,int m2,int s2).
methods.hint: Call the same conversion helper twice before taking the difference.

requirements: Define the specified method(s). Have main call the method that produces the result, using any additional helpers as described.
Read input in the stated order. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: Six integers h1 m1 s1 h2 m2 s2.
details.output: Print the returned result on one line.
constraints: 0 ≤ each hour ≤ 23; 0 ≤ each minute and second ≤ 59.

examples.explanation: The times convert to 3723 and 3785 seconds after midnight. Their absolute difference is 62.
The times convert to 0 and 86399 seconds after midnight. Their absolute difference is 86399.
The times convert to 43200 and 43200 seconds after midnight. Their absolute difference is 0.

methods.title: Two-Tier Utility Charge
methods.task: Return a charge in cents: each of the first threshold units costs lowRate, and each remaining unit costs highRate. There is no fixed charge. Define and call static long utilityCharge(int units,int threshold,int lowRate,int highRate).
methods.hint: Split usage into units within the threshold and units above it.

requirements: Define the specified method(s). Have main call the method that produces the result, using any additional helpers as described.
Read input in the stated order. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: Four integers units, threshold, lowRate, highRate.
details.output: Print the returned result on one line.

examples.explanation: Charge 10 units at 3 cents and 5 at 5 cents: 30 + 25 = 55.
Charge 4 units at 3 cents and 0 at 5 cents: 12 + 0 = 12.
Charge 0 units at 8 cents and 0 at 9 cents: 0 + 0 = 0.

methods.title: Ticket Price by Age and Day
methods.task: baseTicket returns 500 cents for ages below 12, 700 for ages at least 65, and 1000 otherwise. ticketPrice adds a 200-cent weekend fee when weekend is 1. Define and call static int baseTicket(int age); static int ticketPrice(int age,boolean weekend).
methods.hint: Keep the age rule in one helper and add the weekend rule in the other.

requirements: Define the specified method(s). Have main call the method that produces the result, using any additional helpers as described.
Read input in the stated order. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: Two integers age and weekend.
details.output: Print the returned result on one line.

examples.explanation: At age 8, the base price is 500 cents. Add 200 cents for the day, giving 700.
At age 65, the base price is 700 cents. Add 0 cents for the day, giving 700.
At age 30, the base price is 1000 cents. Add 200 cents for the day, giving 1200.

arrays.title: Answer Index Queries
arrays.task: Store the array, then print the value at each requested index, keeping the query order and repetitions.
arrays.hint: Read the array once, then use a[index] for each query.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, then n array integers; then q, followed by q query indices.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 30; −1000 ≤ array values ≤ 1000; 0 ≤ q ≤ 12; 0 ≤ each index < n.

examples.explanation: The queries 2 0 2 select a[2] = 8, a[0] = 4, a[2] = 8. Therefore print '8 4 8'.
The queries (none) select no values. Therefore print ''.
The queries 0 1 select a[0] = -1, a[1] = 0. Therefore print '-1 0'.

arrays.title: Traverse in Reverse
arrays.task: Print the stored array from its final element to its first element without changing the original array.
arrays.hint: Begin at n − 1 and decrement the index while it is at least zero.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Visit indices 2 1 0. They contain '7 -2 4' in that order.
Visit indices (none). They contain '' in that order.
Visit indices 0. They contain '9' in that order.

arrays.title: Sum Even-Numbered Indices
arrays.task: Add values whose zero-based index is even: 0, 2, 4, and so on. The parity of the value itself does not matter.
arrays.hint: Increase the index by 2, beginning at index 0.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The integer sum, or 0 for an empty array.

examples.explanation: Even indices are 0 2 4, with values 5 -3 4. Their sum is 6.
Even indices are none, with values none. Their sum is 0.
Even indices are 0, with values 7. Their sum is 7.

arrays.title: Count a Target Value
arrays.task: Count the array elements equal to target.
arrays.hint: Compare each stored value to target and increase a counter on equality.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then target.
details.output: The occurrence count.

examples.explanation: Target 3 appears at indices 0 2 3. The count is 3.
Target 5 appears at indices none. The count is 0.
Target 8 appears at indices none. The count is 0.

arrays.title: First and Last Target Positions
arrays.task: Find the first and last zero-based indices containing target. Print -1 -1 if the target is absent.
arrays.hint: Set first only on the first match; update last on every match.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then target.
details.output: The first and last indices, separated by a space.

examples.explanation: The matching indices are 0 2 4. Take their endpoints, giving 0 4.
The matching indices are none. Use -1 for both missing positions, giving -1 -1.
The matching indices are 0. Take their endpoints, giving 0 0.

arrays.title: Positions of Minimum and Maximum
arrays.task: Print the indices of the smallest and largest values. For ties, choose the first occurrence of each.
arrays.hint: Keep indices rather than just values, and use strict comparisons to preserve the first tie.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: Minimum index followed by maximum index.

examples.explanation: The minimum -2 first appears at index 1; the maximum 7 first appears at index 2. Print 1 2.
The minimum 9 first appears at index 0; the maximum 9 first appears at index 0. Print 0 0.
The minimum -5 first appears at index 0; the maximum -5 first appears at index 0. Print 0 0.

arrays.title: Build Prefix Totals
arrays.task: Create an array where position i contains the sum of original elements from index 0 through i, inclusive. Print the new array.
arrays.hint: Maintain a running total and store it at every index.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: The prefix calculations are indices 0..0: 3, indices 0..1: 2, indices 0..2: 6. Print '3 2 6'.
The prefix calculations are none because the array is empty. Print ''.
The prefix calculations are indices 0..0: 7. Print '7'.

arrays.title: Sum an Array Interval
arrays.task: Add values from index left through index right, including both endpoints.
arrays.hint: The loop begins at left and must still process right.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then left and right.
details.output: The selected interval sum.

examples.explanation: Indices 1 through 2 contain -2 6. Adding only these values gives 4.
Indices 0 through 0 contain 7. Adding only these values gives 7.
Indices 0 through 2 contain 1 2 3. Adding only these values gives 6.

arrays.title: Adjacent Differences
arrays.task: For every index i from 0 through n − 2, print a[i+1] − a[i]. Arrays shorter than two elements have no differences.
arrays.hint: Stop before the last index because each calculation reads the next element.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: The calculations are 8 − (3) = 5, 6 − (8) = -2. Print '5 -2'.
The calculations are none because no adjacent pair exists. Print ''.
The calculations are none because no adjacent pair exists. Print ''.

arrays.title: Replace Negative Elements
arrays.task: Change every negative array element to zero. Keep zero and positive values unchanged, then print the modified array.
arrays.hint: Assign zero to the same array position when its old value is negative.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Indices 0 3 contain negative values and become 0. The resulting array is '0 0 8 0'.
Indices none contain negative values and become 0. The resulting array is ''.
Indices none contain negative values and become 0. The resulting array is '5 6'.

arrays.title: Scale Every Element
arrays.task: Multiply every array value by factor, store the products in the same array, and print it.
arrays.hint: Use the same multiplication and assignment at every valid index.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then factor.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Multiplying 2 -3 0 by 4 gives '8 -12 0'; each product replaces its original element.
Multiplying (no elements) by 9 gives ''; each product replaces its original element.
Multiplying 5 8 by 0 gives '0 0'; each product replaces its original element.

arrays.title: Swap Two Positions
arrays.task: Exchange the values at indices i and j and print the array. If the indices are equal, leave the array unchanged.
arrays.hint: Save one old value before overwriting its position.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then i and j.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Index 0 holds 4 and index 2 holds 2. Exchanging those positions produces '2 8 4'.
Index 0 holds 7 and index 0 holds 7. Exchanging those positions produces '7'.
Index 1 holds 2 and index 1 holds 2. Exchanging those positions produces '1 2 3'.

arrays.title: Insert One Element
arrays.task: Create a new array with value inserted at index position. The original element at that index and later elements shift right. Insertion at n appends.
arrays.hint: Copy the prefix, write the inserted value, and copy the suffix one position later.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then position and value.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 30; −1000 ≤ values and inserted value ≤ 1000; 0 ≤ position ≤ n.

examples.explanation: The prefix is [2]; insert 9; then copy suffix [4, 6]. The combined result is 2 9 4 6.
The prefix is []; insert 5; then copy suffix []. The combined result is 5.
The prefix is [7, 8]; insert -1; then copy suffix []. The combined result is 7 8 -1.

arrays.title: Delete One Position
arrays.task: Create a new array omitting the element at index position. Keep the order of all other values.
arrays.hint: Use a separate write index, increasing it only when an element is copied.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then position.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Remove index 1, whose value is 4. The remaining values in order are '2 6'.
Remove index 0, whose value is 8. The remaining values in order are ''.
Remove index 2, whose value is 7. The remaining values in order are '5 6'.

arrays.title: Rotate an Array Left
arrays.task: Rotate the array left by k positions: elements leaving the front reappear at the end. Large k may wrap around many times. An empty array stays empty.
arrays.hint: For a nonempty array, reduce k modulo n; output index i reads input index (i+k)%n.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then k.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Reduce 1 modulo 4 to get 1. Move that many leading elements to the end. The result is '2 3 4 1'.
The array is empty, so there is nothing to move. The result is ''.
Reduce 4 modulo 3 to get 1. Move that many leading elements to the end. The result is '8 9 7'.

arrays.title: Reverse a Selected Interval
arrays.task: Reverse the elements from left through right, inclusive, in the existing array. Keep elements outside the interval in place.
arrays.hint: Swap the two endpoints and move both indices inward until they meet or cross.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then left and right.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Only the segment [2, 3, 4] at indices 1..3 reverses to [4, 3, 2]. The entire array becomes 1 4 3 2 5.
Only the segment [7] at indices 0..0 reverses to [7]. The entire array becomes 7.
Only the segment [3, 6, 9] at indices 0..2 reverses to [9, 6, 3]. The entire array becomes 9 6 3.

arrays.title: Copy a Half-Open Slice
arrays.task: Copy elements from start through end − 1 into a new array. The end index is excluded. When start equals end, the slice is empty.
arrays.hint: The slice length is end − start, and source index i maps to destination index i − start.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then start and end.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Read indices 1 2, taking 2 elements. The slice is '4 6'.
Read indices (none), taking 0 elements. The slice is ''.
Read indices (none), taking 0 elements. The slice is ''.

arrays.title: Add Two Arrays by Position
arrays.task: Given arrays a and b of equal length, create result[i] = a[i] + b[i] and print result.
arrays.hint: Use one index to read corresponding elements in both arrays.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, then n integers for array a, then n integers for array b.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: The position-wise sums are 1 + (4) = 5, 3 + (-1) = 2, -2 + (7) = 5. Print '5 2 5'.
The position-wise sums are none. Print ''.
The position-wise sums are 8 + (-8) = 0. Print '0'.

arrays.title: Dot Product of Two Arrays
arrays.task: Multiply corresponding values in equal-length arrays and add all products. The dot product of empty arrays is zero.
arrays.hint: Each index contributes one product to a long accumulator.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, then n integers for array a, then n integers for array b.
details.output: The dot product as an integer.

examples.explanation: The products are 8 -5 6. Adding them from an initial zero gives 9.
The products are none. Adding them from an initial zero gives 0.
The products are 0. Adding them from an initial zero gives 0.

arrays.title: Interleave Equal Arrays
arrays.task: Build a new array in the order a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], and so on.
arrays.hint: Input pair i occupies output positions 2*i and 2*i+1.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, then n integers for array a, then n integers for array b.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Take pairs (1, 9), (2, 8), (3, 7) in order. Flattening those pairs gives '1 9 2 8 3 7'.
Take pairs (none) in order. Flattening those pairs gives ''.
Take pairs (4, -4) in order. Flattening those pairs gives '4 -4'.

arrays.title: Concatenate Two Arrays
arrays.task: Create an array containing all elements of a followed by all elements of b. Either input may be empty.
arrays.hint: The second array starts at destination index n.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n values of a, then m, then m values of b.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Copy 2 values [1, 2] first, then 3 values [7, 8, 9]. The 5-element result is '1 2 7 8 9'.
Copy 0 values [] first, then 1 values [3]. The 1-element result is '3'.
Copy 1 values [4] first, then 0 values []. The 1-element result is '4'.

arrays.title: Even Values before Odd Values
arrays.task: Print all even values in their original order, followed by all odd values in their original order. Zero is even; negative odd values are odd.
arrays.hint: Make one pass for even values and a second pass for odd values.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: The even values in order are [2, 0, 4]; the odd values are [3, -5, 7]. Combining those lists gives '2 0 4 3 -5 7'.
The even values in order are []; the odd values are []. Combining those lists gives ''.
The even values in order are [-2]; the odd values are [-3, -1]. Combining those lists gives '-2 -3 -1'.

arrays.title: Remove Every Target Value
arrays.task: Print the array after removing every occurrence of target. Retain the order of all other elements.
arrays.hint: Only write values that differ from target; track whether a separator is needed.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n array integers, then target.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Removing the 3 occurrence(s) of 2 keeps [1, 3]. Print '1 3'.
Removing the 0 occurrence(s) of 7 keeps []. Print ''.
Removing the 2 occurrence(s) of 4 keeps []. Print ''.

arrays.title: Compare Arrays for Equality
arrays.task: Print YES exactly when the arrays have equal lengths and equal values at every corresponding index; otherwise print NO.
arrays.hint: Check lengths before comparing positions so that every accessed index is valid.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: n, n values of a, then m, then m values of b.
details.output: YES or NO.
constraints: 0 ≤ n,m ≤ 30; −1000 ≤ values ≤ 1000. Do not use Arrays.equals.

examples.explanation: The lengths are 2 and 2. Every corresponding value matches, so print YES.
The lengths are 2 and 2. At least one corresponding value differs, so print NO.
The lengths are 0 and 1. The lengths differ, so print NO.

arrays.title: Check Nondecreasing Order
arrays.task: Print YES if each element after the first is at least its predecessor. Equal neighbors are allowed. Empty and single-element arrays satisfy this rule.
arrays.hint: A single descending adjacent pair disproves the condition.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: YES or NO.

examples.explanation: The adjacent comparisons are -2 ≤ 0 is true, 0 ≤ 0 is true, 0 ≤ 7 is true. Print YES.
The adjacent comparisons are 3 ≤ 2 is false, 2 ≤ 5 is true. Print NO.
The adjacent comparisons are an empty set, so none fails. Print YES.

arrays.title: Count Strict Interior Peaks
arrays.task: Count positions i with both neighbors where a[i] is strictly greater than a[i−1] and a[i+1]. The first and last elements never count.
arrays.hint: Only inspect indices from 1 through n − 2, using strict comparisons on both sides.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The number of strict interior peaks.

examples.explanation: Qualifying indices are 1 3. Thus the peak count is 2.
Qualifying indices are none. Thus the peak count is 0.
Qualifying indices are none. Thus the peak count is 0.

arrays.title: Longest Run of Equal Values
arrays.task: Find the greatest number of consecutive equal elements. Return 0 for an empty array.
arrays.hint: Continue the run when the current value equals the previous one; otherwise start at one.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The longest equal-run length.

examples.explanation: For [2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 3, 2], a changed value starts a new run. The longest equal-valued stretch has 3 element(s). Return 3.
For [], a changed value starts a new run. There are no elements. Return 0.
For [3], a changed value starts a new run. The longest equal-valued stretch has 1 element(s). Return 1.

arrays.title: Check Array Mirror Symmetry
arrays.task: Print YES if reading the array backward gives the same sequence, otherwise NO. Empty arrays are symmetric.
arrays.hint: Compare each position in the first half with n − 1 − i.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: YES or NO.

examples.explanation: The forward sequence is [1, 2, 3, 2, 1] and the backward sequence is [1, 2, 3, 2, 1]. They match, so print YES.
The forward sequence is [1, 2, 3] and the backward sequence is [3, 2, 1]. They differ, so print NO.
The forward sequence is [] and the backward sequence is []. They match, so print YES.

arrays.title: Second Distinct Largest
arrays.task: Print the second largest distinct value. Repeated copies of the largest value do not count as a second value. Print NONE if fewer than two distinct values exist.
arrays.hint: Track two different maxima; ignore a value equal to the current largest.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The second distinct maximum, or NONE.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 30; −10 ≤ values ≤ 10. Use loops; no sorting or sets in the Java solution.

examples.explanation: The distinct values in descending order are [9, 7, 3]. The second entry is 7.
The distinct values in descending order are [5]. There is no second entry, so return NONE.
The distinct values in descending order are [-1, -3, -4]. The second entry is -3.

arrays.title: Values above the Mean
arrays.task: Print the values strictly greater than the arithmetic mean of the whole array, preserving order. For an empty array, print an empty line. Avoid floating-point calculations.
arrays.hint: For nonempty arrays, compare value*n with the total sum.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: The sum is 12 and length is 3. Select values with value × 3 > 12. The selected values are '7'.
The array is empty, so no mean comparison is needed. The selected values are ''.
The sum is -8 and length is 4. Select values with value × 4 > -8. The selected values are '1'.

arrays.title: Compress Consecutive Duplicates
arrays.task: Keep the first value of each consecutive run of equal values. Equal values separated by a different value are retained separately.
arrays.hint: Keep index 0 and every later value that differs from its predecessor.

requirements: Read the n values into an int[] array and solve using basic loops or indexing.
Indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result, with no prompts.
input: An integer n followed by n integers.
details.output: The requested integers on one line, separated by one space; an empty result is an empty line.

examples.explanation: Keep indices 0 2 5, where new runs begin. The retained sequence is '2 3 2'.
Keep indices none, where new runs begin. The retained sequence is ''.
Keep indices 0, where new runs begin. The retained sequence is '3'.

arrays.title: Sum Immediate Neighbors
arrays.task: Create a new array where each position contains the sum of its immediate left and right neighbors in the original array. A missing neighbor contributes zero. Do not include the value at the position itself.

requirements: Store and process the sequence using ArrayList<Integer>.
Begin with an empty queue. PUSH value adds at the back; POP removes and prints the front value; PEEK prints the front without removing it. POP or PEEK on an empty queue prints EMPTY.
All indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result.
input: q followed by q commands, one per line.
details.output: Print one response per POP or PEEK, then QUEUE followed by final values from front to back. Print only QUEUE when empty.
constraints: 0 <= q <= 16; every pushed value is -20 through 20.

examples.explanation: Commands [] give operation responses []; the final queue record is 'QUEUE'.
Commands [('PUSH', 4), ('PUSH', 7), ('PEEK',), ('POP',), ('PEEK',)] give operation responses ['4', '4', '7']; the final queue record is 'QUEUE 7'.
Commands [('POP',), ('PEEK',), ('PUSH', -20), ('POP',), ('POP',)] give operation responses ['EMPTY', 'EMPTY', '-20', 'EMPTY']; the final queue record is 'QUEUE'.

arraylist.title: Group values into nested lists
arraylist.task: Create an ArrayList of ArrayLists by splitting the input into consecutive groups of at most k values. All groups except possibly the last contain exactly k values.
arraylist.hint: Start a new inner list at indices 0,k,2k,... and stop the final group at size.

requirements: Store and process the sequence using ArrayList<Integer>.
Create an ArrayList of ArrayLists by splitting the input into consecutive groups of at most k values. All groups except possibly the last contain exactly k values.
All indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result.
input: n and n integers, followed by positive group size k.
details.output: Print the number of groups, then each group on its own line with values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Splitting [] into groups of at most 1 gives [].
Splitting [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] into groups of at most 2 gives [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]].

arraylist.title: Circular elimination order
arraylist.task: People labeled 1 through n stand in a circle. Starting at label 1, count k people inclusively and remove the kth. Continue counting from the next remaining person, wrapping around, until one survives.
arraylist.hint: After removing index i, the next survivor already occupies index i in the shortened list.

requirements: Store and process the sequence using ArrayList<Integer>.

People labeled 1 through n stand in a circle. Starting at label 1, count k people inclusively and remove the kth. Continue counting from the next remaining person, wrapping around, until one survives.
All indices are zero-based. Print only the requested result.
input: Two integers: n k.
details.output: Print eliminated labels in order on the first line, which is empty for n=1. Print the surviving label on the second line.

examples.explanation: With n=1 and k=1, elimination order is ''; the surviving label is 1.

With n=30 and k=50, elimination order is '20 11 4 29 26 25 28 3 10 19 6 22 15 13 16 24 9 5 8 23 21 7 14 17 27 18 1 12 2'; the surviving label is 30.

linkedlist-api.title: Process removal requests

linkedlist-api.hint: Later requests see the list left by earlier requests.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.

details.output: Print the successful-removal count, then the final list or EMPTY on the next line.

linkedlist-api.hint: Track a gap index; insertion increases it but deleting to its right does not.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: The first integer n is the number of values.
The next n integers are the values in their original order.
Next is q, followed by q commands LEFT, RIGHT, ADD x, or DELETE.
details.output: Print the final cursor position on one line. Print the final list or EMPTY on the next line.
constraints: Inserted and initial values are between -100 and 100.

examples.explanation: Start with [] and gap 0. Commands [] leave cursor and list as 0 / EMPTY.
Start with [1, 2] and gap 0. Commands [('RIGHT',), ('ADD', 9), ('DELETE',)] leave cursor and list as 2 / 1 9.
Start with [-1] and gap 0. Commands [('LEFT',), ('DELETE',), ('DELETE',), ('RIGHT',)] leave cursor and list as 0 / EMPTY.

linkedlist-api.title: Merge sorted linked lists
linkedlist-api.task: Merge two nondecreasing LinkedLists into one nondecreasing list. Repeatedly take the smaller front value; on equal values, take from the first list. Keep every duplicate.
linkedlist-api.hint: Compare only the two front values until one list becomes empty.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n and its n sorted integers.
Read m and its m sorted integers.
details.output: Print the resulting values in list order, separated by one space. Print EMPTY for an empty list.

examples.explanation: Merging the sorted values [] and [] while retaining duplicates gives EMPTY.
Merging the sorted values [-3, 2, 2] and [0, 2, 7] while retaining duplicates gives -3 0 2 2 2 7.
Merging the sorted values [] and [-1, 4] while retaining duplicates gives -1 4.

linkedlist-api.title: Finish jobs by round-robin service
linkedlist-api.task: Jobs are numbered 1..n in input order. Put them into a LinkedList queue. On each turn, give the front job up to quantum units of work. A completed job leaves; otherwise move it to the back with its remaining work. Report completion order.
linkedlist-api.hint: Store each job number together with its remaining work.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, then n positive required-work amounts.
The final integer is the positive quantum.
details.output: Print completed job numbers in completion order, separated by spaces; print EMPTY when there are no jobs.

examples.explanation: Jobs have work amounts [] and each turn allows 3 units. Cycling unfinished jobs to the back makes them finish in order EMPTY.
Jobs have work amounts [2] and each turn allows 5 units. Cycling unfinished jobs to the back makes them finish in order 1.
Jobs have work amounts [5, 1, 4] and each turn allows 2 units. Cycling unfinished jobs to the back makes them finish in order 2 3 1.

linkedlist-api.title: Record circular elimination order
linkedlist-api.task: Place participants numbered 1..n in a queue. Each round starts counting at the front as 1: move the first k-1 participants, one at a time, from front to back, then remove the front participant. Continue until the queue is empty.
linkedlist-api.hint: Use removeFirst plus addLast for each counted participant who stays.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: The input contains n and k.
details.output: Print all removed participant numbers in removal order, or EMPTY when n is zero.

examples.explanation: With participants 1 through 0 and every 3th front-counted participant removed, the removal order is EMPTY.
With participants 1 through 1 and every 7th front-counted participant removed, the removal order is 1.
With participants 1 through 5 and every 2th front-counted participant removed, the removal order is 2 4 1 5 3.

hashmap.title: Keep the latest assignment for each key
hashmap.task: Store the assignments in a HashMap. Display the final mapping.
hashmap.hint: put replaces the value for an existing key. Sort a copy of keySet before printing.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n lines containing integer key and value. Apply assignments in input order; a later assignment to the same key replaces its old value.
details.output: Print one key value pair per line, with keys in increasing order. Print EMPTY if the map is empty.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: Applying [] in order leaves {}. Printing its keys in increasing order gives EMPTY.
Applying [(4, 7)] in order leaves {4: 7}. Printing its keys in increasing order gives 4 7.
Applying [(2, 5), (-1, 3), (2, 9)] in order leaves {2: 9, -1: 3}. Printing its keys in increasing order gives -1 3 / 2 9.

hashmap.title: Look up a key safely
hashmap.task: Build the map, then look up key k. A stored zero is a real value, not a missing entry.
hashmap.hint: Use containsKey to distinguish a missing key from a stored zero.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n lines containing integer key and value. Apply assignments in input order; a later assignment to the same key replaces its old value.
The final integer is k.
details.output: Print its value, or MISSING if the key is absent.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: After assignments the map is {}. Looking up key 4 returns MISSING.
After assignments the map is {2: 3, 4: 9}. Looking up key 2 returns 3.
After assignments the map is {1: -4, 3: 8}. Looking up key 7 returns MISSING.

hashmap.title: Report the value replaced by put
hashmap.task: Build the map, then call put(k,v). Report the old value and the final map.
hashmap.hint: put returns the previous value, or null for a new key.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n lines containing integer key and value. Apply assignments in input order; a later assignment to the same key replaces its old value.
The final line contains k and v.
details.output: Print the old value, or MISSING if k was absent. Then print the final map in increasing key order, one key value pair per line.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: Key 2 previously held MISSING. Assigning 8 yields MISSING / 2 8.
Key 1 previously held 4. Assigning -3 yields 4 / 1 -3 / 2 7.
Key 3 previously held MISSING. Assigning 0 yields MISSING / 0 0 / 3 0.

hashmap.title: Remove a map entry and report it
hashmap.task: Build the map, then remove key k. Removing an absent key leaves the map unchanged.
hashmap.hint: remove(key) returns the previous value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n lines containing integer key and value. Apply assignments in input order; a later assignment to the same key replaces its old value.
The final integer is k.
details.output: Print the removed value or MISSING on the first line. Then print the remaining map in increasing key order, or EMPTY.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.

hashmap.title: Find a stored value
hashmap.task: Build the map and determine whether any entry has value x. Only final values count after replacements.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.

The final integer is x.
details.output: Print YES if any current entry has value x; otherwise print NO.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.

hashmap.task: Process key-value records with putIfAbsent so the first value for each key is kept.
hashmap.hint: putIfAbsent ignores later assignments to a key that already exists.

hashmap.task: Count how many times each input integer appears using a HashMap.

hashmap.hint: Use String keys and sort a copy of the keys for output.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n nonempty words.
details.output: Print word count pairs in Java String alphabetical order (uppercase letters before lowercase letters), one pair per line. Print EMPTY if n is zero.
constraints: Each word contains 1 to 12 English letters.

examples.explanation: Tokens [] are counted exactly as written. The alphabetically ordered counts are EMPTY.
Tokens ['pear'] are counted exactly as written. The alphabetically ordered counts are pear 1.
Tokens ['red', 'blue', 'red', 'Red'] are counted exactly as written. The alphabetically ordered counts are Red 1 / blue 1 / red 2.

hashmap.title: Accumulate totals for each key
hashmap.task: Each record adds amount to its key's running total. A new key starts at zero. Keep keys whose final total is zero.
hashmap.hint: merge(key,amount,Integer::sum) adds to the current total.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n integer key amount pairs.
details.output: Print one key value pair per line, with keys in increasing order. Print EMPTY if the map is empty.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: Add every amount belonging to the same key in []. The resulting totals are EMPTY.
Add every amount belonging to the same key in [(4, 7)]. The resulting totals are 4 7.
Add every amount belonging to the same key in [(2, 5), (-1, 3), (2, 9)]. The resulting totals are -1 3 / 2 14.

hashmap.title: Keep the largest reading for each key
hashmap.task: For each key, retain the largest value among its records. Negative readings are valid.
hashmap.hint: Do not initialize maxima to zero; a key may have only negative readings.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n integer key reading pairs.
details.output: Print one key value pair per line, with keys in increasing order. Print EMPTY if the map is empty.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: Compare only readings with equal keys in []. Keeping each group's largest value gives EMPTY.
Compare only readings with equal keys in [(4, 7)]. Keeping each group's largest value gives 4 7.
Compare only readings with equal keys in [(2, 5), (-1, 3), (2, 9)]. Keeping each group's largest value gives -1 3 / 2 9.

hashmap.title: Store the most recent position
hashmap.task: For each distinct input value, store the zero-based index where it appeared most recently.
hashmap.hint: Overwrite the stored index whenever the value appears again.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: The first integer n is the number of values.
The next n integers are the values in their original order.
details.output: Print value lastIndex pairs in increasing value order, or EMPTY.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: In [], the last seen zero-based position is stored for each value. These value-position pairs are EMPTY.
In [5], the last seen zero-based position is stored for each value. These value-position pairs are 5 0.
In [3, -2, 3, 0, -2], the last seen zero-based position is stored for each value. These value-position pairs are -2 4 / 0 3 / 3 2.

hashmap.title: Group all positions by value
hashmap.task: Create a HashMap from each input value to a list of all of its zero-based positions, in increasing position order.
hashmap.hint: computeIfAbsent creates the position list only the first time a value appears.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: The first integer n is the number of values.
The next n integers are the values in their original order.
details.output: Print one row per distinct value in increasing value order: the value followed by all its positions. Print EMPTY for no input values.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: Value groups collect positions from left to right in []. Printing groups by increasing value gives EMPTY.
Value groups collect positions from left to right in [5]. Printing groups by increasing value gives 5 0.
Value groups collect positions from left to right in [3, -2, 3, 0, -2]. Printing groups by increasing value gives -2 1 4 / 0 3 / 3 0 2.

hashmap.title: Invert a map with a collision rule
hashmap.task: First build the final map from the assignments. Then create an inverse HashMap from each old value to an old key. If multiple old keys share a value, keep the smallest old key.
hashmap.hint: Use merge with Math.min so collisions do not depend on map iteration order.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n lines containing integer key and value. Apply assignments in input order; a later assignment to the same key replaces its old value.
details.output: Print oldValue smallestOldKey pairs in increasing oldValue order. Print EMPTY if the original map is empty.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: The final original map is {}. Group its keys by stored value and choose the smallest key in each group: EMPTY.
The final original map is {4: 7}. Group its keys by stored value and choose the smallest key in each group: 7 4.
The final original map is {2: 9, -1: 3}. Group its keys by stored value and choose the smallest key in each group: 3 -1 / 9 2.

hashmap.title: Merge two maps by addition
hashmap.task: Build each map independently, keeping its latest assignment per key. Merge the second map into the first by adding values for shared keys and inserting new keys. Keep zero totals.
hashmap.hint: Finish both maps before merging; repeated assignments within one map replace rather than add.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.

Read m followed by m key value pairs for the second map.
details.output: Print one key value pair per line, with keys in increasing order. Print EMPTY if the map is empty.
constraints: Every sequence has 0 to 30 integers unless a stricter bound is stated.
Each integer value is between -100 and 100.
All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

examples.explanation: The two final maps are {} and {}. Add values for shared keys, giving EMPTY.

The two final maps are {0: 0} and {0: -2}. Add values for shared keys, giving 0 -2.

hashmap.title: Remove entries below a threshold
hashmap.task: Build the map, then remove every entry whose final value is less than threshold. A value equal to threshold is kept.
hashmap.hint: removeIf can test each entry's current value.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.

details.output: Print one key value pair per line, with keys in increasing order. Print EMPTY if the map is empty.

All input is valid and integers are separated by whitespace.

hashmap.title: Rank the highest map entries
hashmap.task: Build the map, then select up to k entries with highest final values. A tie is resolved by smaller key.
hashmap.hint: Sort keys using both the value rule and the key tie-breaker.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Read n, followed by n lines containing integer key and value. Apply assignments in input order; a later assignment to the same key replaces its old value.

details.output: Print selected key value pairs, one per line, ordered by decreasing value then increasing key. Print EMPTY if k is zero or the map is empty.
constraints: Keys and values are between -100 and 100.

examples.explanation: The final map is {}. Rank its entries by value descending and key ascending, then take at most 0: EMPTY.

The final map is {4: -3, 1: -5}. Rank its entries by value descending and key ascending, then take at most 8: 4 -3 / 1 -5.

hashmap.title: Choose the most frequent integer
hashmap.task: Count the values with a HashMap and find the one with greatest frequency. On a frequency tie, choose the smaller integer.
hashmap.hint: Compare frequency first and integer value second.

The next n integers are the values in their original order.
