priorityqueue.hint: Copy on both SAVE and RESTORE; assigning the same queue reference would let later polls destroy the checkpoint.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer q, followed by q commands.
ADD x takes one integer. SAVE, RESTORE, and TAKE take none.
details.output: Print one line for every query command, then the final collection on its own line. Print EMPTY for an empty list.
constraints: Every command follows the listed grammar.

examples.explanation: The checkpoint starts empty. Following no commands copies contents at SAVE/RESTORE, so TAKE results and the final queue are EMPTY.

examples.input:
6
RESTORE
TAKE
ADD 7
SAVE
TAKE
RESTORE
examples.explanation: The checkpoint starts empty. Following RESTORE; TAKE; ADD 7; SAVE; TAKE; RESTORE copies contents at SAVE/RESTORE, so TAKE results and the final queue are EMPTY / 7 / 7.

examples.input:
8
ADD 4
ADD 1
SAVE
TAKE
ADD 9
RESTORE
TAKE
RESTORE
examples.explanation: The checkpoint starts empty. Following ADD 4; ADD 1; SAVE; TAKE; ADD 9; RESTORE; TAKE; RESTORE copies contents at SAVE/RESTORE, so TAKE results and the final queue are 1 / 1 / 1 4.

priorityqueue.title: Change the priority of one record
priorityqueue.task: Each record has a distinct id and priority. Update the priority of the requested id if it exists; otherwise change nothing. Poll by increasing priority, then increasing id. Remove the record before changing its comparator key, then reinsert it.
priorityqueue.hint: Mutating a queued priority does not automatically reorder the queue. Remove, update, and offer again.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
Then n rows: id priority.
Finally targetId newPriority.
details.output: Print IDs in the new polling order, or EMPTY.

examples.explanation: Updating ID 1 to priority 4 yields records []. Their (priority, id) poll order is EMPTY.
Updating ID 1 to priority -1 yields records [(1, -1)]. Their (priority, id) poll order is 1.
Updating ID 3 to priority 0 yields records [(1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 0)]. Their (priority, id) poll order is 3 1 2.

priorityqueue.title: Compute statistics without assuming iteration order
priorityqueue.task: Iterate over a priority queue once to count entries, sum all values with long arithmetic, and count negative entries. Print count, sum, and negativeCount. Then poll and print the minimum or EMPTY. Statistics must not depend on iterator order.
priorityqueue.hint: Iteration is suitable for order-independent statistics; only poll guarantees the priority head.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
details.output: Print count sum negativeCount on line 1 and the polled minimum or EMPTY on line 2.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: All 0 values sum to 0; 0 are negative. Iteration removes none, so the final poll returns EMPTY.
All 1 values sum to 7; 0 are negative. Iteration removes none, so the final poll returns 7.
All 6 values sum to 13; 2 are negative. Iteration removes none, so the final poll returns -2.

comparator.title: Compare two integers without overflow
comparator.task: Compare a with b in natural numeric order. Print LESS, EQUAL, or GREATER according to the sign of Integer.compare(a,b).
comparator.hint: Do not return a-b: subtraction can overflow. Only the comparison sign matters.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two signed 32-bit integers a and b.
details.output: Print LESS, EQUAL, or GREATER.

examples.explanation: Compare -2147483648 with 2147483647 numerically. The first is smaller, so print LESS.
Compare 7 with 7 numerically. The first is equal, so print EQUAL.
Compare 9 with -4 numerically. The first is larger, so print GREATER.

comparator.title: Sort using a natural comparator
comparator.task: Sort all integers in ascending numeric order with Comparator.naturalOrder. Keep repeated values.
comparator.hint: List.sort accepts a comparator; equal values remain repeated.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Ordering EMPTY from smallest to largest gives EMPTY. All 0 entries are retained.
Ordering 7 from smallest to largest gives 7. All 1 entries are retained.
Ordering 4 -2 4 0 -2 9 from smallest to largest gives -2 -2 0 4 4 9. All 6 entries are retained.

comparator.title: Reverse an existing numeric comparator
comparator.task: Create an ascending integer comparator, reverse it with reversed(), and sort the input in descending numeric order. Keep duplicates.
comparator.hint: Reverse the comparator instead of negating input values, which fails for Integer.MIN_VALUE.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: The reversed natural comparator places larger values first. Applied to EMPTY, it produces EMPTY.
The reversed natural comparator places larger values first. Applied to 7, it produces 7.
The reversed natural comparator places larger values first. Applied to 4 -2 4 0 -2 9, it produces 9 4 4 0 -2 -2.

comparator.title: Break absolute-value ties numerically
comparator.task: Sort by increasing absolute magnitude, then increasing signed value. The absolute magnitude of -2147483648 is 2147483648 and must fit in long.
comparator.hint: Widen to long before Math.abs, and use thenComparingInt for equal magnitudes.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: The (magnitude, value) keys are []. Sorting these keys gives EMPTY.
The (magnitude, value) keys are [(7, 7)]. Sorting these keys gives 7.
The (magnitude, value) keys are [(4, 4), (2, -2), (4, 4), (0, 0), (2, -2), (9, 9)]. Sorting these keys gives 0 -2 -2 4 4 9.

comparator.title: Group parity before sorting within groups
comparator.task: Sort even numbers before odd numbers. Within each parity group sort numerically ascending. Negative odd values belong to the odd group.
comparator.hint: Math.floorMod(x,2) gives 0 or 1 even for negative x.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Even entries sort as EMPTY; odd entries sort as EMPTY. Concatenating the groups gives EMPTY.
Even entries sort as EMPTY; odd entries sort as 7. Concatenating the groups gives 7.
Even entries sort as -2 -2 0 4 4; odd entries sort as 9. Concatenating the groups gives -2 -2 0 4 4 9.

comparator.title: Sort by distance from a chosen target
comparator.task: Sort values by increasing distance from target x; break equal-distance ties by the smaller numeric value. Compute each difference in long.
comparator.hint: Casting after subtraction is too late; write Math.abs((long)v-target).

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A signed 32-bit target x.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Relative to -1000000000, the (distance, value) keys are []. Their order is EMPTY.
Relative to 0, the (distance, value) keys are [(7, 7)]. Their order is 7.

comparator.title: Order words by length and spelling
comparator.task: Sort shorter words first. For equal lengths use Java natural case-sensitive lexicographic order; uppercase English letters precede lowercase letters.

comparator.title: Place enclosing intervals before contained ties
comparator.task: Sort interval rows by start ascending. When starts tie, put larger ends first. Identical intervals may appear more than once and all copies remain. Print each interval as start:end.
comparator.hint: Give the endpoint tie-breaker its own reversed comparator.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.

details.output: Print start:end tokens separated by spaces, or EMPTY.

examples.explanation: Rows [] sort by (start, -end). Thus equal starts place the enclosing interval first: EMPTY.

comparator.title: Compare two long values safely
comparator.task: Compare two signed 64-bit integers with Long.compare. Print LESS, EQUAL, or GREATER. Avoid both subtraction and casting the difference to int.
comparator.hint: Long.compare returns an int sign while comparing the original long operands.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two signed 64-bit integers a and b.
details.output: Print LESS, EQUAL, or GREATER.

examples.explanation: The first long is -9223372036854775808 and the second is 9223372036854775807. Their numeric relation is LESS without computing a difference.
The first long is 9223372036854775807 and the second is 9223372036854775807. Their numeric relation is EQUAL without computing a difference.
The first long is 9000000000000000000 and the second is -1. Their numeric relation is GREATER without computing a difference.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.

collections.title: Swap two selected list positions
collections.task: For a nonempty list, exchange the values at zero-based positions i and j with Collections.swap. If n is zero, i and j are both 0 and the operation is defined to do nothing.
collections.hint: Swapping an index with itself is valid; avoid any index access for an empty list.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
First zero-based index i.
Second zero-based index j.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: For n > 0, 0 <= i,j < n. For n = 0, i = j = 0.

examples.explanation: There are no positions to exchange; after the specified swap the list is EMPTY.
Position 0 holds 7 and position 0 holds 7; after the specified swap the list is 7.
Position 0 holds 4 and position 4 holds -2; after the specified swap the list is -2 -2 4 0 4 9.

collections.title: Report the natural minimum and maximum
collections.task: Use Collections.min and Collections.max to report the smallest and largest values without changing list order. Print EMPTY for no values; otherwise print min max on one line.
collections.hint: Both utility methods require a nonempty collection, so guard the empty case first.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
details.output: Print min max, or EMPTY when n is zero.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Among EMPTY, there is no minimum or maximum. Print EMPTY.
Among 7, the smallest value is 7 and the largest is 7. Print 7 7.
Among 4 -2 4 0 -2 9, the smallest value is -2 and the largest is 9. Print -2 9.

collections.title: Count all occurrences with frequency
collections.task: Print Collections.frequency(list,x): the total number of entries equal to x. Every duplicate occurrence contributes one.
collections.hint: frequency counts equal objects, not just distinct membership.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
The signed 32-bit value x to count.
details.output: Print one nonnegative count.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Value 4 appears at zero-based positions []. There are 0 occurrences.
Value 7 appears at zero-based positions [0]. There are 1 occurrences.
Value 4 appears at zero-based positions [0, 2]. There are 2 occurrences.

collections.title: Check whether two collections are disjoint
collections.task: Use Collections.disjoint to determine whether A and B share no equal values. Print DISJOINT when there is no shared value, otherwise OVERLAP. Duplicate counts do not affect the answer.
collections.hint: An empty collection is disjoint from every collection, including another empty collection.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
The next n integers form A; the next m integers form B.
details.output: Print the requested result. Separate list items with spaces and use EMPTY for an empty list.

examples.explanation: The shared distinct values are EMPTY. Therefore the collections are DISJOINT.
The shared distinct values are EMPTY. Therefore the collections are DISJOINT.
The shared distinct values are EMPTY. Therefore the collections are DISJOINT.

collections.title: Replace all matching values and report a match
collections.task: Use Collections.replaceAll(list,oldValue,newValue). Print YES if at least one oldValue was found, otherwise NO. Then print the updated list. When oldValue equals newValue, a found occurrence still makes the result YES.
collections.hint: The boolean reports whether a matching element existed, not whether the visible contents differ.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
The value to find.
The replacement value.
details.output: Print YES or NO on line 1, then the updated list on line 2.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: There are 0 occurrences of 7. Replacing each with 7 yields the match flag and list NO / EMPTY.
There are 1 occurrences of 7. Replacing each with 0 yields the match flag and list YES / 0.
There are 2 occurrences of 4. Replacing each with -1000000000 yields the match flag and list YES / -1000000000 -2 -1000000000 0 -2 9.

collections.title: Fill existing positions with one value
collections.task: Use Collections.fill to replace every existing list position with x. Preserve the list size. An empty list stays empty because fill does not append elements.
collections.hint: fill replaces elements using set; it does not grow the list.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A signed 32-bit fill value x.
details.output: Print the filled list on line 1, then the unchanged size on line 2.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: There are 0 existing positions. Replacing each with -1000000000 gives EMPTY, while the size stays 0.
There are 1 existing positions. Replacing each with 0 gives 0, while the size stays 1.
There are 6 existing positions. Replacing each with -1000000000 gives -1000000000 -1000000000 -1000000000 -1000000000 -1000000000 -1000000000, while the size stays 6.

collections.title: Copy a source over an existing destination
collections.task: Use Collections.copy(destination,source). The destination already has at least as many positions as the source. Replace its opening positions with the source; preserve the remaining destination suffix. Print destination and unchanged source.
collections.hint: Capacity is not size: Collections.copy needs actual destination elements to overwrite.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m, the destination and source sizes.
Then n destination integers followed by m source integers.
details.output: Print the updated destination on line 1 and the unchanged source on line 2; use EMPTY for an empty list.

examples.explanation: Overwrite the first 0 of 0 destination positions with EMPTY. Its surviving suffix is EMPTY; the two lists print as EMPTY / EMPTY.
Overwrite the first 1 of 1 destination positions with 9. Its surviving suffix is EMPTY; the two lists print as 9 / 9.
Overwrite the first 2 of 4 destination positions with 8 9. Its surviving suffix is 3 4; the two lists print as 8 9 3 4 / 8 9.

collections.title: Create repeated values with nCopies
collections.task: Create Collections.nCopies(n,x), an immutable list containing n copies of integer x. Print its contents and size. A zero count creates an empty list.
collections.hint: nCopies creates a list of the requested size, unlike reserving ArrayList capacity.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Two integers n and x.
details.output: Print the repeated list on line 1 and its size on line 2.

examples.explanation: Repeat 7 exactly 0 times to get EMPTY. The resulting size is 0.
Repeat 7 exactly 1 times to get 7. The resulting size is 1.
Repeat 4 exactly 3 times to get 4 4 4. The resulting size is 3.

collections.title: Append an array through Collections.addAll
collections.task: Convert B to an Integer array and append all of its elements to mutable list A with Collections.addAll. Print YES if A changed, otherwise NO, followed by the updated A. Duplicates are appended normally.
collections.hint: For an ArrayList, adding a nonempty array changes the list even if all values already occur.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
The next n integers form A; the next m integers form B.
details.output: Print the requested result. Separate list items with spaces and use EMPTY for an empty list.

examples.explanation: Append 0 entries EMPTY to EMPTY. The change flag and final list are NO / EMPTY.
Append 0 entries EMPTY to 7. The change flag and final list are NO / 7.
Append 2 entries 8 -2 to 4 1 4. The change flag and final list are YES / 4 1 4 8 -2.

collections.title: Decode a natural-order binary search
collections.task: Remove exact duplicates and sort numerically ascending, then call Collections.binarySearch for x. Print the search list and the returned index. A missing value returns -(insertionPoint)-1, using a zero-based insertion point.
collections.hint: Removing duplicates gives each present search value exactly one possible index.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A signed 32-bit search key x.
details.output: Print the unique sorted list on line 1, then the binary-search return value on line 2.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

collections.title: Find the first contiguous sublist
collections.task: Use Collections.indexOfSubList(A,B) to find the first zero-based start of B as a contiguous sublist of A. Print -1 if absent. An empty B matches at position 0.
collections.hint: A match must be contiguous and preserve every repeated value; this is not containsAll.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
Then n values of A, followed by m values of B.
details.output: Print one zero-based match index, or -1.

The matching start positions for 2 inside 2 are [0]. The first match rule gives 0.

collections.title: Find the last contiguous sublist
collections.task: Use Collections.lastIndexOfSubList(A,B) to find the last zero-based start of B as a contiguous sublist of A. Print -1 if absent. An empty B matches at A.size().
collections.hint: A match must be contiguous and preserve every repeated value; this is not containsAll.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
Then n values of A, followed by m values of B.
details.output: Print one zero-based match index, or -1.

The matching start positions for 2 inside 2 are [0]. The last match rule gives 0.

collections.title: Shuffle reproducibly with a seeded Random
collections.task: Apply Collections.shuffle to the ArrayList with new Random(seed). Use the standard backwards shuffle: for i from size down to 2, swap index i-1 with Random.nextInt(i). Print the resulting permutation.
collections.hint: Pass the supplied seed to java.util.Random; creating an unseeded Random makes the answer vary.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A signed 32-bit random seed.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Starting from EMPTY, seed 0 determines every backwards shuffle swap. The reproducible permutation is EMPTY; its values and multiplicities are unchanged.
Starting from 7, seed 7 determines every backwards shuffle swap. The reproducible permutation is 7; its values and multiplicities are unchanged.
Starting from 4 -2 4 0 -2 9, seed 42 determines every backwards shuffle swap. The reproducible permutation is -2 4 -2 9 0 4; its values and multiplicities are unchanged.

collections.title: Rotate only a selected sublist
collections.task: Apply Collections.rotate to the backed view list.subList(lo,hi). Positive k rotates the selected range right and negative k rotates it left. Positions outside the half-open range [lo,hi) stay in place.
collections.hint: A subList is a view of the parent, so rotating the view updates that parent range.

collections.title: Reverse a half-open range through its view
collections.task: Reverse list.subList(lo,hi) using Collections.reverse. The view shares the parent list, so only the positions in [lo,hi) reverse. Empty ranges have no effect.
collections.hint: hi is exclusive; there are exactly hi-lo selected positions.

collections.title: Distinguish an unmodifiable view from a snapshot
collections.task: Create an unmodifiable view of the input list and an unmodifiable snapshot made from a fresh copy. Append x to the original mutable list. Print the view, then the snapshot. Attempt to append through the view and print BLOCKED when UnsupportedOperationException is thrown.

collections.title: Copy an immutable singleton before appending
collections.task: Create Collections.singletonList(x). Attempt to append y directly and catch UnsupportedOperationException, printing BLOCKED. Then make a mutable ArrayList copy and append y successfully. Print the unchanged singleton and the mutable copy.
collections.hint: A mutable copy has its own container; successful changes to it do not modify the singleton.

details.output: Print a line for each TEXT or SIZE command, then the final integer list, or EMPTY.

collections.title: Observe a set backed by a supplied map
collections.task: Start with an empty HashMap<Integer,Boolean>, create a set using Collections.newSetFromMap, and add all input values through the set. Remove x directly from the backing map. Print YES if that map removal found x, otherwise NO. Then print remaining set values in increasing order.
collections.hint: The supplied map must be empty when creating the set; later changes through either view share the same entries.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A signed 32-bit map key x to remove.
details.output: Print YES/NO on line 1, then the remaining sorted set on line 2.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: Adding the inputs creates distinct members EMPTY. Removing map key -1000000000 finds no entry, and the set now contains EMPTY.
Adding the inputs creates distinct members 7. Removing map key 7 finds it, and the set now contains EMPTY.
Adding the inputs creates distinct members -2 0 4 9. Removing map key -1000000000 finds no entry, and the set now contains -2 0 4 9.

collections.title: Remove every member of a forbidden collection
collections.task: Call A.removeAll(B). Remove every A occurrence equal to any B value; B multiplicities do not limit removal. Preserve survivor order. Print YES if A changed, otherwise NO, followed by the updated A.
collections.hint: removeAll is membership-based: one forbidden value removes all of its copies from A.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
The next n integers form A; the next m integers form B.
details.output: Print the requested result. Separate list items with spaces and use EMPTY for an empty list.

examples.explanation: The forbidden distinct values are EMPTY. Removing every matching occurrence from EMPTY gives the flag and survivors NO / EMPTY.
The forbidden distinct values are EMPTY. Removing every matching occurrence from 7 gives the flag and survivors NO / 7.
The forbidden distinct values are -2 8. Removing every matching occurrence from 4 1 4 gives the flag and survivors NO / 4 1 4.

collections.title: Retain every member of an allowed collection
collections.task: Call A.retainAll(B). Keep every A occurrence equal to any B value, preserving A order. Values absent from B are removed; B multiplicities do not limit retention. Print whether A changed, then the retained list.
collections.hint: Retain membership, not one-for-one matches; two A copies survive even if B has one.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
The next n integers form A; the next m integers form B.
details.output: Print the requested result. Separate list items with spaces and use EMPTY for an empty list.

examples.explanation: The allowed distinct values are EMPTY. Retaining matching A entries gives NO / EMPTY.
The allowed distinct values are EMPTY. Retaining matching A entries gives YES / EMPTY.
The allowed distinct values are -2 8. Retaining matching A entries gives YES / EMPTY.

collections.title: Delete a range through a backed sublist
collections.task: Call list.subList(lo,hi).clear() to remove exactly the half-open range [lo,hi) from the parent list. The surviving prefix and suffix join without changing their internal order.
collections.hint: Clear the range view itself; do not structurally modify the parent while continuing to use a stale view.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A zero-based inclusive lower bound lo.
A zero-based exclusive upper bound hi.
details.output: Print the requested integers separated by spaces; print EMPTY for an empty result.

examples.explanation: Remove positions 0 through -1, containing EMPTY. Joining the surviving prefix and suffix gives EMPTY.
Remove positions 1 through 0, containing EMPTY. Joining the surviving prefix and suffix gives 7.
Remove positions 0 through 5, containing 4 -2 4 0 -2 9. Joining the surviving prefix and suffix gives EMPTY.

collections.title: Replace through an array-backed fixed-size list
collections.task: Convert the input to an Integer array and wrap it with Arrays.asList. If nonempty, replace position index with x through the list view. Print the backing array. Attempt to append x through the view and catch UnsupportedOperationException, printing BLOCKED. For n=0, index=0 and no replacement occurs.
collections.hint: Arrays.asList supports set because size is unchanged; add is unsupported because the backing array cannot grow.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A zero-based replacement index, or 0 when n is zero.
A signed 32-bit replacement value x.
details.output: Print the backing array contents on line 1, then BLOCKED on line 2.
constraints: For n > 0, 0 <= index < n; otherwise index = 0.

examples.explanation: The empty array has no replaceable position. The array prints EMPTY; growing the view is BLOCKED.
Replacing index 0 changes the backing array value to 10. The array prints 10; growing the view is BLOCKED.
Replacing index 0 changes the backing array value to 99. The array prints 99 -2 4 0 -2 9; growing the view is BLOCKED.

collections.title: Verify that toArray makes a detached container
collections.task: Export the list using toArray(new Integer[0]). If the array is nonempty, set its first slot to x. Append x to the original list. Print the exported array and then the original list, showing that changes to either container do not resize or replace positions in the other.
collections.hint: The exported array is a separate container; these Integer elements are immutable values.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A signed 32-bit value x.
details.output: Print the exported array on line 1 and the updated original list on line 2.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: The array’s first slot is absent, giving EMPTY. Appending to the source independently gives -1000000000.
The array’s first slot becomes 0, giving 0. Appending to the source independently gives 7 0.
The array’s first slot becomes -1000000000, giving -1000000000 -2 4 0 -2 9. Appending to the source independently gives 4 -2 4 0 -2 9 -1000000000.

collections.title: Distinguish ordered equality from multiset equality
collections.task: First compare A.equals(B), which requires matching positions and multiplicities. Then sort independent copies and compare them to test equality of multisets. Print YES or NO for ordered equality, then YES or NO for multiset equality.
collections.hint: List.equals is order-sensitive; sorting copies aligns equal multiset occurrences while preserving the originals.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
Then n values of A followed by m values of B.
details.output: Print two YES/NO lines: ordered equality, then multiset equality.

examples.explanation: A is EMPTY and B is EMPTY. Their position-by-position result is YES; their sorted forms EMPTY and EMPTY give multiset result YES.
A is 7 and B is 7 7. Their position-by-position result is NO; their sorted forms 7 and 7 7 give multiset result NO.
A is 4 1 4 and B is 4 4 1. Their position-by-position result is NO; their sorted forms 1 4 4 and 1 4 4 give multiset result YES.

collections.title: Check whether a list has enough copies
collections.task: Treat A as available inventory and B as requested values. Print YES only when A has at least as many copies of every value as B requests. Use Collections.frequency for multiplicity checks; containsAll alone is insufficient.
collections.hint: For each distinct request, compare its frequency in both lists without consuming either list.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: Integers n and m.
Then n available values A followed by m requested values B.
details.output: Print YES if every requested multiplicity is available, otherwise NO.

examples.explanation: Available counts are {}; requested counts are {}. The missing counts are {}, so print YES.
Available counts are {2: 1}; requested counts are {2: 2}. The missing counts are {2: 1}, so print NO.
Available counts are {3: 2, 1: 1}; requested counts are {3: 2}. The missing counts are {}, so print YES.

collections.title: Use a deque through a LIFO queue view
collections.task: Create an ArrayDeque and wrap it with Collections.asLifoQueue. Offer every input value through the queue view in input order, then poll at most k values. Print the polled values and the backing deque from front to back. New offers go to the deque front.
collections.hint: asLifoQueue maps offer to the deque front, so the last offered value is polled first.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n.
The next n space-separated integers are the list, in input order.
A maximum poll count k (0 <= k <= 30).
details.output: Print polled values on line 1 and the remaining backing deque on line 2; use EMPTY as needed.
constraints: Each list value is a signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: After offering EMPTY, the deque front-to-back order is EMPTY. Polling up to 0 values gives EMPTY / EMPTY for removed values and remaining backing deque.
After offering 7, the deque front-to-back order is 7. Polling up to 1 values gives 7 / EMPTY for removed values and remaining backing deque.
After offering 4 -2 4 0 -2 9, the deque front-to-back order is 9 -2 0 4 -2 4. Polling up to 3 values gives 9 -2 0 / 4 -2 4 for removed values and remaining backing deque.

collections.hint: Dispatch each command to the corresponding Collections method; every operation preserves the list size.

requirements: Read the input in the given order. Print only the requested answer, with no prompts or extra labels.
input: An integer n followed by n list integers.
Then an integer q followed by q commands.
Commands are SORT, REVERSE, ROTATE k, FILL x, REPLACE old new, and SHOW.
details.output: Print one list line for each SHOW command, then one final list line. Use EMPTY for an empty list.
constraints: All list, fill, and replacement values are signed 32-bit integers.

examples.explanation: Start from EMPTY and apply SHOW. Each SHOW observes all earlier changes; snapshots and the final state print as EMPTY / EMPTY.
Start from 7 and apply FILL 2; SHOW. Each SHOW observes all earlier changes; snapshots and the final state print as 2 / 2.
Start from 4 -2 4 0 and apply REVERSE; ROTATE -1; REPLACE 4 9; SHOW; SORT. Each SHOW observes all earlier changes; snapshots and the final state print as 9 -2 9 0 / -2 0 9 9.
